Subject: Re: Residency confirmation + archival sunset questions (Dedicated)

Alice — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: yes, tenant data for Dedicated clusters is region-bound by default; and we have a documented archival/sunset process with configurable retention windows. See details below and attached evidence draft.

High-level summary:
- Region pinning: requests, KV cache, model inputs, and tenant snapshots are stored on-host in the designated region and are not cross-region replicated unless you enable cross-region backups. We enforce this at the orchestration and storage layer.
- Backups/snapshots: customers can configure snapshot schedules and a separate cross-region backup toggle. By default snapshots remain in the same region in cold storage.
- Deletion/sunset: delete requests trigger a multi-step purge: mark-for-deletion -> asynchronous scrub of active storage -> snapshot tombstone + cold storage expiry -> final sweep and audit log entry. Typical completion for active storage scrub: 0–24 hours; cold storage purge follows retention TTL (configurable: 30/90/365 days).

I've attached: geobind_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook excerpt), audit-log-sample-202505.csv (sample scrub audit), and a retention matrix we discussed.

Next steps: Laura, Aditya — can you validate the backup/replication wording below and confirm the artefact chain we can provide as evidence to FinSecure (screenshot/drive link + audit snippet)? Karthik — can you add estimated timelines for cold storage purge and whether we provide a signed attestation?

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick technical clarification and what we can hand over as evidence.

Replication model:
- The Dedicated control plane enforces placement constraints; block storage (local NVMe or regional EBS depending on node type) is provisioned in-region. We do not create hot replicas in other regions.
- Cross-region backups are an opt-in at the tenant level and are explicitly visible in the tenant config and billing.

Evidence we can provide now (samples attached / links):
- Runbook excerpt with ops steps and deletion playbook (geobind_runbook_v1.pdf).
- Sample scrub audit (audit-log-sample-202505.csv) that shows tombstone events and job ids.
- Snapshot retention matrix (snapshot-retention-matrix.xlsx) describing TTLs and cold-store lifecycle.
- Optional: a redacted log dump that shows node IDs, timestamps, and cluster region tags (we can provide redacted sample for review).

Deletion timeline notes:
- Active storage scrub (index and block-level trimming): usually completes within 24 hours for typical tenant sizes; large-footprint tenants may take longer and we surface status in the deletion job tracker.
- Cold storage purge: dependent on configured retention TTL. After the retention TTL expires we run an irrevocable purge within a maintenance window; evidence includes purge job id, S3 object deletion markers, and final audit entry.

Action items:
- Michael: confirm whether we will provide a signed attestation PDF for legal.
- Aditya: prepare a redacted log dump (sanitized) we can hand to FinSecure demonstrating region tags and deletion job ids.
- Karthik: confirm whether backup snapshots are stored under a separate, auditable bucket with region constraints and provide the retention enforcement mechanism briefly.

Laura Bennett
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
